errors.text: The proposed NbTaTiV-like refractory nanoparticles are materially distinct from the AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles, eliminating the element-specific Au/Cu surface segregation and evaporation mechanism central to the target.
Severe lattice distortion effects on dislocation motion are incorrectly used as evidence for sluggish atomic self-diffusion; these are different kinetic processes.
The claimed <20 nm threshold and 200–300°C stability reduction are not supported by the cited evidence.
The predicted phase separation or amorphization replaces the target outcome of surface-energy-driven Au/Cu shell formation, melting, evaporation, reshaping, and loss of small particles.
